title: 480. The French Revolution: The Rights of Man (Part 6)

sentences.en: The representatives of the French people formed into a national assembly and considering ignorance,
sentences.zh: 法国人民的代表们组成国民议会，考虑到对人权的无知、

sentences.en: forgetfulness or contempt of the rights of man to be the only causes of public misfortunes and the corruption of governments have resolved to set forth in a solemn declaration the natural,
sentences.zh: 忘却或蔑视是公众不幸和政府腐败的唯一原因，乃决定在一项庄严的宣言中阐明人类自然的、

sentences.en: unalienable and sacred rights of man.
sentences.zh: 不可剥夺的和神圣的权利。

sentences.en: To the end, that this declaration, constantly present to all members of the body politic, may remind them unceasingly of their rights and their duties.
sentences.zh: 以便这一宣言时刻提醒政治共同体的所有成员，使他们不断铭记自己的权利与义务。

sentences.en: The duties.
sentences.zh: 那些义务。

sentences.en: Who saw that coming?
sentences.zh: 谁能预料到这一点？

sentences.en: So, Tom, that is the preamble to the declaration of the rights of man and of the citizen.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，这就是《人权和公民权宣言》的序言。

sentences.en: I'm now rethinking everything I thought about the French Revolution because Margaret Thatcher, in our first episode, told us they forgot about the duties, but they didn't.
sentences.zh: 我正在重新思考我对法国大革命的所有看法，因为玛格丽特·撒切尔在我们的第一期节目中告诉我们，他们把义务给忘了，但其实他们没有。

sentences.en: I'm in shock.
sentences.zh: 我惊呆了。

sentences.en: Only in the preamble, though, they didn't include the duties in the list of rights that follow that.
sentences.zh: 不过，仅限于序言部分，他们并没有把义务列入随后的权利清单中。

sentences.en: Oh, that is the giveaway.
sentences.zh: 哦，这正是破绽所在。

sentences.en: So people who are wondering what we're talking about, that is the preamble to the Declaration of the Rights of Man and the Citizen,
sentences.zh: 所以，那些好奇我们在谈论什么的人，这就是《人权和公民权宣言》的序言，

sentences.en: one of the landmark documents in all human history.
sentences.zh: 人类历史上最具里程碑意义的文件之一。

sentences.en: It was approved by the National Assembly on the 26th of August, 1789.
sentences.zh: 它于1789年8月26日获得国民议会批准。

sentences.en: And Tom, they had been talking about it for about a month, hadn't they?
sentences.zh: 而且汤姆，他们大约讨论了一个月，不是吗？

sentences.en: This document that now we all think of is so tremendously important.
sentences.zh: 这份如今在我们看来如此极其重要的文件。

sentences.en: Why did they feel they needed it?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们觉得需要它呢？

sentences.en: Well, you say that it's a document that we're all familiar with.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你说这是一份我们都很熟悉的文件。

sentences.en: I'm not entirely confident in the English-speaking world that that's the case.
sentences.zh: 我在英语世界里并没有完全的信心认为事实确实如此。

sentences.en: You mentioned Mrs Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 你提到了撒切尔夫人。

sentences.en: We looked at the beginning about how she talked about how the French Revolution, the ideals, the values, the principles,
sentences.zh: 我们在开头探讨过她是如何谈论法国大革命、那些理想、价值观、原则，

sentences.en: all these were already evident in Britain's glorious revolution and the kind of the Whig-ish tradition of parliamentary democracy and all that.
sentences.zh: 所有这些在英国的光荣革命、辉格党传统的议会民主制以及诸如此类的事情中都已经显现出来了。

sentences.en: And I think also for American listeners, they will be thinking of the Declaration of Independence, that the Declaration of Independence came firSt.
sentences.zh: 我想对于美国听众来说，他们也会想到《独立宣言》，即《独立宣言》是先出来的。

sentences.en: And I think for that reason that English speakers tend perhaps, and I certainly speak for myself,
sentences.zh: 我想正因为如此，讲英语的人可能倾向于——而且我当然是在说我自己——

sentences.en: it doesn't tend to kind of dominate my imaginings in the way that I think it does certainly for the
sentences.zh: 它不像在我看来对法国人那样，也不像对世界各地的人那样，主导着我的想象力。

sentences.en: French, but also for people across the world.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为直到这个时间点，多米尼克，在上一集中，你把攻占巴士底狱描绘成一个充满流血和暴力的故事。

sentences.en: Because I think until this point, Dominic, in the previous episode, you portrayed the Fall of the Bastille as a story of bloodshed and kind of violence.
sentences.zh: 而你通过模仿滑稽的法国口音，来表达你对这份具有图腾意义的人权宣言的敬意。

sentences.en: And you've shown your respect for this totemic declaration of human rights by putting on a comedy French accent.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得法国大革命是一个关于理想、原则和价值观的故事。

sentences.en: But I think the French Revolution is a story of ideals and principles and values.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说其中没有令人难以置信的暴力。

sentences.en: And that's not to say that there isn't incredible violence.
sentences.zh: 显然是有的。

sentences.en: There obviously is.
sentences.zh: 我认为暴力和理想主义是交织在一起的。

sentences.en: I think that the violence and the idealism are intertwined.
sentences.zh: 它们是水乳交融的。

sentences.en: They're interfused.
sentences.zh: 不理解其中之一，就不可能理解另一个。

sentences.en: It's impossible to understand the one without the other.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你只强调暴力，却不指出人们非常非常认真看待的那些抽象名词，那么我认为你就

sentences.en: And so if you just emphasize the violence without saying, there are a lot of abstract nouns that people take very, very seriously, then I think you're
sentences.zh: 既忽略了法国大革命发生的方式，也忽略了——当然，非常重要的一点——一直延续到当代的深远遗产。

sentences.en: missing out on both why the French Revolution happens in the way that it does, and also, of course, very importantly, the enduring legacy right the way into the present day.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很公道，汤姆，因为暴力是由对抽象名词的信仰驱动的，对吧？

sentences.en: I think that's fair enough, Tom, because the violence is driven by belief in the abstract nouns, right?
sentences.zh: 这不是为了暴力而暴力。

sentences.en: It's not violence for its own sake.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有时也许是的，但人们真心相信他们所宣扬的意识形态。

sentences.en: I mean, sometimes it may be, but people genuinely believe in the ideology they're preaching.
sentences.zh: 而这种意识形态，我是说，它赋予了他们一种信念，我猜，让他们觉得他们所做的是对的。

sentences.en: And that ideology, I mean, it gives them a faith, I suppose, that what they're doing is right.
sentences.zh: 我们将在本集节目中探讨它在多大程度上是一种信仰。

sentences.en: We will be exploring the degree to which it's a faith over the course of this episode.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为对于法国大革命的崇拜者来说，当然也对于法国国家而言，它是伟大的宣言。

sentences.en: Because I think that for admirers of the French Revolution, and of course, for the French state as well, it is the great manifesto.
sentences.zh: 它的影响和辐射是彻底震撼性的。

sentences.en: And it's completely seismic in its implications and its influence.
sentences.zh: 事实上在法国，它的重要性至今仍在法兰西第五共和国——也就是现今这个共和国——宪法的序言中得到明确承认。

sentences.en: And actually in France, its significance is explicitly acknowledged to this day in the preamble to the constitution of the fifth republic, the current kind of republic.
sentences.zh: 如果你回想一下在1989年法国大革命二百周年之际的所有那些世界领导人，

sentences.en: And if you think about all those world leaders who in the bicentenary of the French revolution in
sentences.zh: 除了撒切尔夫人之外，他们都在称赞大革命所主张的价值观，那种自由的、世俗的、平等的价值观。

sentences.en: 1989, who weren't Mrs. Thatcher, they were all praising the revolution for the values that they said it upheld, the kind of the liberal, secular, egalitarian values.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以能够这样做，正如你在上一集结尾时所提到的，这些价值观虽然具有鲜明的法国特色，但它们也被塑造为具有普遍意义。

sentences.en: And they were able to do that because, as you mentioned at the end of the previous episode, these values, although they are specifically French, they are also cast as universal.
sentences.zh: 因此，法国大革命能够把自己塑造成一盏照亮了全世界的明灯。

sentences.en: And so the French revolution is able to cast itself as a fire that has illumined the entire world.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，《人权和公民权宣言》对世界其他地方的共和制宪法产生了巨大影响。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the Declaration of the Rights of Man and the Citizen has been massively influential on other Republican constitutions around the world.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为最主要的是对联合国《世界人权宣言》的影响，该宣言非常有启示意义地于1949年在巴黎通过。

sentences.en: And I think preeminently on the UN's Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which was adopted very tellingly, I think, in 1949 in Paris.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以理解为什么《人权和公民权宣言》的热情拥护者对它提出了极高的主张。

sentences.en: So you can see why enthusiasts for the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen make very high claims for it indeed.
sentences.zh: 我来读一下乔纳森·伊斯雷尔（Jonathan Israel）在他的关于法国大革命的书《革命思想》中所说的话。

sentences.en: So I'll just read you what Jonathan Israel in his book on the French Revolution, Revolutionary Ideas, says.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·伊斯雷尔是那种观点的狂热拥护者和倡导者，他认为法国大革命源于他所说的激进启蒙运动，

sentences.en: And Jonathan Israel is the great enthusiast and proponent of the notion that the French Revolution kind of emerges from what he calls the radical enlightenment,
sentences.zh: 即无神论的启蒙运动、对君主制和宗教的激进敌视等等。

sentences.en: the enlightenment of atheism, of radical hostility to monarchy and religion and so on.
sentences.zh: 在谈到《人权宣言》时，他说，人类历史上第一次，平等、个人自由、受国家平等保护的权利，

sentences.en: And he says, talking about the Declaration of the Rights of Man, for the first time in history, equality, individual liberty, the right to equal protection by the state,
sentences.zh: 以及思想和言论自由，被奉为所有公正和理性社会所固有的基本原则。

sentences.en: and freedom of thought and expression were enshrined as basic principles declared inherent in all just and rational societies.
sentences.zh: 民主现代性的基石已经奠定。

sentences.en: The bedrock of democratic modernity was in place.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你对此怎么看？

sentences.en: What do you make of that, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是反驳的观点，不是吗？针对伯克式的观点，

sentences.en: Well, that's the counter-argument, isn't it, to the slightly Burkean argument,
sentences.zh: 埃德蒙·伯克的观点，即他在恐怖统治发生之前就出版的《法国革命论》。

sentences.en: Edmund Burke's argument, his reflections on the revolution in France, which was published even before the terror.
sentences.zh: 伯克说，这太可怕了，抛弃了传统和习俗。

sentences.en: Burke said, this is terrible, throwing out traditions and custoMs.
sentences.zh: 你们将陷入无政府状态和恐怖之中。

sentences.en: You'll be left with anarchy and horror.
sentences.zh: 甚至在当时，也有很多人对伯克说，你忽略了这样一个事实，即这将真正带来一个新世界，

sentences.en: And even at the time, there were a lot of people who said to Burke, you are missing the fact that this will genuinely bring in a new world,
sentences.zh: 一个由自由和人类理性表达所主导的自由世界。

sentences.en: a liberal world governed by freedom and by the expression of human reason.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是乔纳森·伊斯雷尔所论证的，不是吗？

sentences.en: And that's effectively what Jonathan Israel is arguing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想在根本上是的。

sentences.en: I think in the fundamentals, yes.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们讨论那些抽象名词之前——我们将会探讨它们，因为我认为它们对理解革命的进程至关重要，

sentences.en: So before we get on to the abstract nouns, which we will be looking at, because I think they are so important to understanding the course of the revolution,
sentences.zh: 我们是不是应该先回顾一下，提醒自己我们当时身处何地？

sentences.en: Should we just go back and remind ourselves where we were?
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在哪里？

sentences.en: Yes, where are we?
sentences.zh: 所以我们有了国民议会，它是先前三个等级合并而成的。

sentences.en: So we've got the National Assembly, which is the conflation of what had previously been the three estates.
sentences.zh: 现在，国民议会成为了人民意志和主权的化身。

sentences.en: Now, the National Assembly is the embodiment of the will and the sovereignty of the people.
sentences.zh: 巴士底狱已经陷落。

sentences.en: The Bastille has fallen.
sentences.zh: 第一批流亡贵族已经逃离。

sentences.en: The first émigrés have fled.
sentences.zh: 而没有逃跑的路易，正试图把自己重新包装成一位立宪君主。

sentences.en: And Louis, who has not fled, is trying to reinvent himself as a constitutional monarch.
sentences.zh: 但正当这一切发生的时候，所有引发革命的诱因，

sentences.en: But while all this is going on, everything that precipitated the revolution,
sentences.zh: 也就是主要的因素：没有钱，面包价格极高，这些其实并没有真正改变。

sentences.en: So chiefly, the fact that there's no money and that the bread price is very high, that hasn't really changed.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以仍然有一种恐慌和危机的气氛，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so there's still an atmosphere of panic and crisis, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 所以问题来了。

sentences.en: So here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 为什么身处国民议会的代表们，

sentences.en: Why are the deputies who are in the National Assembly,
sentences.zh: 当你们会觉得他们的首要任务应该是讨论面包供应或其他什么事情时，他们却把所有时间都用来讨论《人权宣言》？

sentences.en: why would they spend all their time talking about a Declaration of Human Rights when you would think their priority would be to be discussing bread supplies or whatever it might be?
sentences.zh: 因为我认为，大多数在1789年5月汇聚到凡尔赛的代表——也就是为了三级会议而后转变为国民议会的人，

sentences.en: Because I think that most of the deputies who had assembled at Versailles in May 1789, so for the Estates General that then becomes the National Assembly,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们认为自己来到那里是为了给法国一部新宪法。

sentences.en: I mean, they thought that they had come there to give France a new constitution.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他们的运作假设是，除非你为这个国家奠定新的基础，否则你无法治愈法国面临的弊病。

sentences.en: And I think they operate on the assumption that you can't remedy the ills facing France unless you have set the country on new foundations.
sentences.zh: 而《权利宣言》是一次尝试，旨在为代表们自己以及法国所有人民勾勒出一种理解，即从今以后

sentences.en: And the Declaration of Rights is an attempt to frame for both the delegates themselves, but also for all the people of France, an understanding of what henceforward
sentences.zh: 将是什么在激励着新的法国。

sentences.en: will be animating the new France.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这实际上是一种被攻占巴士底狱极大地催化了的理解。

sentences.en: And I think that that is actually an understanding that is turbocharged by the fall of the Bastille.
sentences.zh: 因为你刚才说国民议会中的人们其实对所发生的事情感到困扰。

sentences.en: Because you were saying how the people in the National Assembly are actually perturbed by what happens.
sentences.zh: 他们对此感到不安。

sentences.en: They're unsettled by it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我说得没错吧，随着数周过去，在他们思考这件事的同时，传来的消息——与其说是来自巴黎，

sentences.en: And actually, I'm right in saying, aren't I, that as the weeks go by, so during the time they're thinking about this, the news coming in, not so much from Paris,
sentences.zh: 不如说是来自乡村——比以往任何时候都更加惊人，可以说是法国历史上前所未有的令人震惊，

sentences.en: but from the countryside, is more alarming than ever, and arguably more alarming than ever before in French history,
sentences.zh: 因为这一年被历史学家称为“大恐惧”（la grande peur）之年。

sentences.en: because this is the year of what historians call la grande peur, the great fear.
sentences.zh: 所以这些消息是从各省传来的。

sentences.en: So this is coming in from the provinces.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，其中既有希望也有恐惧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think there's hope as well as fear.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经提到过他了，阿瑟·扬，这个去法国旅行的英国人。

sentences.en: So we've already mentioned him, Arthur Young, this Englishman who's gone on a trip across France.
sentences.zh: 是的，一次时机糟糕的度假。

sentences.en: Yeah, an ill-timed holiday.
sentences.zh: 是的，一次时机糟糕的旅行。

sentences.en: Yeah, an ill-timed trip.
sentences.zh: 所以他在攻占巴士底狱前两天身处洛林，遇到了一位农妇，他问，你知道的，你过得怎么样？

sentences.en: So he, two days before the fall of the Bastille, is in Lorraine and he meets a peasant woman and he asks, you know, how are you doing?
sentences.zh: 他写下了她所说的话。

sentences.en: And he writes what she said.
sentences.zh: 当时据说大人物们会为像我们这样的穷人做点什么，但她不知道是谁，也不知道怎么做。

sentences.en: It was said at present that something was to be done by some great folks for such poor ones, but she did not know who nor how.
sentences.zh: 但愿上帝赐予我们更好的生活，因为财产税和封建捐税正在压垮我们。

sentences.en: But God send us better because property taxes and feudal dues are crushing us.
sentences.zh: 而阿瑟·扬为了说明穷人正被压在他们身上的重担所压垮，他猜测这个女人一定有60或70岁了。

sentences.en: And Arthur Young, as a kind of illustration of the way that the poor are being crushed by the weight on them, he assumes that this woman must be kind of 60 or 70.
sentences.zh: 但他一问，结果她才28岁。

sentences.en: But he asks and she turns out to be 28.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 但随后巴士底狱陷落了，实际上，这并没有让乡村的温度降下来。

sentences.en: But then the Bastille falls, and that actually, it doesn't lessen the temperature in the countryside.
sentences.zh: 它实际上，你知道的，让温度飙升到了极点，因为人们现在开始听说一座堡垒已经陷落，

sentences.en: It actually, you know, it sends it through the roof because people now start, they hear that one fortress has fallen
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始攻击其他的权威堡垒，对吧？

sentences.en: and they start to attack other citadels of authority, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们在焚烧登记册。

sentences.en: And they're burning the registers.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，我认为这才是关键。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, that's the key, I think.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我认为攻占巴士底狱被报道为封建主义的灭亡。

sentences.en: I think the fall of the Bastille is reported as the fall of feudalism.
sentences.zh: 我们再次在上一集中提到过，这非常像是农民起义。

sentences.en: And we, again, mentioned this in the previous episode, it's very peasants' revolt.
sentences.zh: 有这样一种想法：如果你作为一个农民，能够烧毁那些注定让你只能当农民的登记册和特许状，那么你就会获得自由。

sentences.en: There's this idea that if you, as a peasant, can burn the registers and the charters that condemn you to work as a peasant, then you will be free.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始将目标对准城堡，特别是修道院和男女修道院，正如农民起义的日子里一样，它们也拥有大片土地。

sentences.en: And so they start targeting chateaux and particularly abbeys and monasteries, which also, you know, as in the days of the peasant revolt, own large tracts of land.
sentences.zh: 这也随之带来了封建捐税和什一税。

sentences.en: And this brings kind of feudal dues and tithes with them.
sentences.zh: 遭到袭击的一个修道院的例子是勃艮第的一座，名叫瑟纳宗（Senazon）。

sentences.en: So an example of an abbey that gets attacked is one in Burgundy called Senazon.
sentences.zh: 这座修道院被完全夷为平地，它属于当地一个非常显赫的家族，即塔лей兰-佩里戈尔（Talleyrand-Perigord）家族。

sentences.en: And this is completely leveled and it belongs to a very distinguished local family, the family of Talleyrand-Perigord.
sentences.zh: 这个家族最著名的成员实际上是一位主教，即当地城镇欧坦（Autun）的主教。
